5: \section{Setup and motivation}
6: \label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7: 
8: Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9: integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10: Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11: \cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12: set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13: \'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14: \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15: representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16: packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17: 
18: \medskip
19: 
20: \textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21: constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22: different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23: 
24: The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25: Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26: as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27: relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28: (\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29: Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30: \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31: relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32: of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33: 
34: The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35: separably closed field, from the open loci
36: \[
37:   C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38: \]
39: cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40: points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41: before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42: pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43: classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme. Its structure, and the parts of it that
44: are established, are the subject of \cref{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar}.
45: 
46: The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
47: quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
48: the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
49: (\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
50: only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
51: that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
52: Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
53: mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
54: consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
55: 
56: \medskip
57: 
58: \textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
59: the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
60: works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
61: \(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
62: representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
63: \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
64: Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
65: and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
66: (automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
67: base change), then the comparison maps
68: \[
69:   \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
70:   \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
71: \]
72: are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
73: plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
74: allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
75: 
76: The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
77: even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
78: \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
79: formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
80: 
81: \begin{enumerate}
82:   \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
83:     hypothesis. This is the formulation of
84:     \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
85:     in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
86:     proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
87:     rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
88:     over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
89:     hypothesis.
90:   \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
91:     rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
92:     precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
93:     would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
94:     the \'etale site.
95: \end{enumerate}
96: 
97: Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
98: being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
99: side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
100: 
101: Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
102: rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
103: \cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
104: 
105: % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4 (FGA Explained Ch.~9 \S 9.4);
106: % arXiv:math/0504020, p.~26. Read from
107: % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex.
108: 
109: \section{Line bundles and the Quot / Hilbert scheme}
110: \label{sec:fga_pic_line_bundle_quot}
111: 
112: The bridge from line bundles on \(C \times_k T\) to the Quot scheme is the
113: Abel map: a relative effective divisor \(D \subset C \times_k T\) over \(T\)
114: (a \(T\)-flat closed subscheme whose ideal is invertible) determines a closed
115: subscheme of \(C \times_k T\) flat over \(T\), hence a \(T\)-point of the Hilbert
116: functor \(\Hilb_{C/k}(T)\), which is the special case \(\Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\)
117: of the Quot functor of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}; and it determines an
118: invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\) on the relative curve,
119: representing a class in \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T)\).
120: 
121: \begin{definition}[Abel-map witness]\leanok
122:   \label{def:abel_map_witness}
123:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.abelMapWitness}
124:   \uses{def:div_functor_carrier, def:pic_sharp_carrier}
125:   Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper curve. Define a
126:   natural transformation
127:   \[
128:     A^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C/k} \colon \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}
129:       \longrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}
130:   \]
131:   as the composite
132:   \(
133:     \mathrm{abelKernelNatTrans}(C)
134:     \mathbin{;} \mathrm{picNeg}(C)
135:   \).
136: \end{definition}
137: 
138: \begin{proof}\leanok
139:   The first transformation sends the class represented by
140:   \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) to \([\ker q]\). It is well defined because
141:   equivalent divisor families induce isomorphic kernels. It is natural under
142:   arbitrary base change because the kernel--pullback comparison is an
143:   isomorphism for an epimorphic quotient with finitely presented, base-flat
144:   target and invertible kernel. The second transformation is pointwise
145:   inversion in the group-valued presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\). Their composite
146:   is therefore natural and sends
147:   \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) to \(-[\ker q]\).
148: \end{proof}
149: 
150: \begin{lemma}[Line bundle / Quot correspondence via the Abel map]\leanok
151:   \label{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}
152:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk}
153:   \uses{def:abel_map_witness, def:inst_has_abel_map, def:has_abel_map,
154:     def:div_functor_carrier, def:pic_sharp_carrier}
155:   % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 3, Def.~dfn:Abel (the Abel
156:   % map), and Thm.~th:repDiv (representability of relative effective
157:   % divisors by an open subscheme of \(\IHilb_{X/S}\)); arXiv:math/0504020,
158:   % pp.~25, 23 (read from
159:   % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex, L1837-L1841 + L2135-L2145).
160:   % Source identifiers: \begin{thm}\label{th:repDiv}\end{thm}
161:   % and \begin{dfn}\label{dfn:Abel}\end{dfn}.
162:   \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 3,
163:   Thm.~3.7 + Def.~4.6 (cf.\ [Nitsure], ``Construction of Hilbert
164:   and Quot Schemes'', \S 1, where \(\Hilb_{X/S} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_X/X/S}\)).}
165:   Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. There is a
166:   natural transformation of presheaves on \((\Sch/k)^{op}\)
167:   \[
168:     A_{C/k} = \mathrm{abelMap} \;\colon\; \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}
169:       \;\longrightarrow\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}
170:   \]
171:   (\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) the relative-divisor functor of
172:   \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}, \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) the relative
173:   Picard functor of \cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}), with the following
174:   \emph{defining property}: at a \(T\)-point represented by a family
175:   \(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\) (\cref{def:div_family}: a finitely
176:   presented, \(T\)-flat quotient
177:   \(q \colon \mathcal O_{C\times_kT}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F\)
178:   whose kernel is an invertible ideal sheaf cutting out a relative effective
179:   divisor \(D\subseteq C\times_kT\)),
180:   \[
181:     A_{C/k}(T)\bigl(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\bigr)
182:       \;=\; -[\ker q] \;=\; [(\ker q)^{-1}]
183:       \;=\; \bigl[\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\bigr]
184:       \;\in\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T),
185:   \]
186:   the class of the associated invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k
187:   T}(D)\), i.e.\ the additive inverse of the class of the ideal sheaf
188:   \(\ker q\) (Kleiman \S 3, Def.~dfn:Abel). This transformation is the
189:   required witness for \(\mathrm{HasAbelMap}(C)\)
190:   (\cref{def:has_abel_map}).
191: \end{lemma}
192: 
193: \begin{proof}
194:   The instance of \cref{def:inst_has_abel_map} identifies
195:   \(A_{C/k}\) with the witness of \cref{def:abel_map_witness}. Evaluating its
196:   two factors at \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) first gives the kernel class
197:   \([\ker q]\) and then its inverse. Since the kernel is the ideal sheaf of
198:   \(D\), its inverse is \(\mathcal O_{C\times_kT}(D)\), which gives the stated
199:   formula.
200: \end{proof}
201: 
202: \begin{remark}
203: [Representability of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)]
204:   \label{rem:div_functor_representability}
205:   Kleiman~\S 3, Thm.~th:repDiv, shows that \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) is
206:   representable by an open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \subseteq
207:   \Hilb_{C/k}\) of the Hilbert scheme (\(\Hilb_{C/k} =
208:   \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\), \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}): letting
209:   \(W \subseteq C \times_k \Hilb_{C/k}\) be the universal closed
210:   subscheme and \(q \colon W \to \Hilb_{C/k}\) the projection, the locus
211:   \(V \subseteq W\) where \(W\) is locally an effective Cartier divisor
212:   is open, so \(Z := q(W \setminus V)\) is closed (\(q\) proper) and
213:   \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} := \Hilb_{C/k} \setminus Z\) is the open
214:   subscheme representing relative effective divisors. This is
215:   the relative-divisor functor appearing in
216:   \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}.
217: \end{remark}
218: 
219: \section{The FGA representability theorem}
220: \label{sec:fga_pic_representability}
221: 
222: We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck's existence theorem
223: for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian:
224: \(S = \Spec k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral
225: curve. The general theorem (Kleiman \S 4, Thm.~4.8) covers any
226: \(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric
227: fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise.
228: 
229: \begin{theorem}[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]\leanok
230:   \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}

The presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) is generally not an \'etale (or even Zariski)
sheaf. The standard obstruction (Kleiman \S 2, L1292--L1302): for a \(k\)-scheme
\(T\) carrying a non-trivial line bundle whose pullback to \(C \times_k T\) becomes
non-trivial after an open cover, the Zariski separated-presheaf condition
fails. Therefore, to obtain a representable functor in the sense of
\cref{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}, one must replace
\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) by its \emph{associated \'etale sheaf}. Kleiman \S 2 names
this sheaf \(\Pic_{(X/S)\et}\) and singles it out as the functor that Kleiman's
main existence theorem in \S 4 represents.
